{
  "extractions": [
    {
      "unit": "F001:F004",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001"],
        "scope_text": "Applies to an employee of a covered employer seeking to be an eligible employee under the FMLA.",
        "context_quotes": ["F000"],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": ["F002", "F003", "F004"],
        "choice_quote": "F001:F004",
        "choice_text": "All three requirements must be met: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months, (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding leave commencement, and (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.",
        "logic_quote": "F001:F004",
        "references": ["§ 825.801", "§ 825.105(b)"],
        "statement": "An eligible employee is defined as an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special rules for airline flight crew employees in § 825.801), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees working outside the U.S.)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F005",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F002"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": ["F006"],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F005",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided the rules in paragraph (b) are met."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F006",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2).",
        "context_quotes": ["F007:F009"],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F006",
        "references": ["paragraph (b)(2)"],
        "statement": "Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2), employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F007:F009",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005", "F007"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, where an employee had a break in service of more than seven years.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": ["F008", "F009"],
        "choice_quote": "F007:F009",
        "choice_text": "Either (i) the break in service is occasioned by USERRA-covered service obligation, or (ii) a written agreement exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.",
        "logic_quote": "F007:F009",
        "references": ["USERRA", "38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."],
        "statement": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where: (i) the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation (and the period of absence due to USERRA service must also be counted, without granting greater entitlement than USERRA), or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F002", "F005"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F010",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, the week counts as a week of employment; for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed equal to 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005"],
        "scope_text": "When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "Nothing in this section prevents",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Employers may consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement, but if an employer chooses to recognize such prior employment, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F003"],
        "scope_text": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees, in determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": ["paragraph (c)(2)", "§ 825.801", "FLSA", "29 CFR part 785"],
        "statement": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to FLSA principles for compensable hours of work based on actual hours worked; the determination is not limited by recordkeeping methods or inaccurate compensation agreements, and any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA principles may be used."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F003"],
        "scope_text": "When determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave for an employee returning from USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "shall",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": ["USERRA", "§ 825.801(c)"],
        "statement": "An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the absence due to USERRA service to meet the hours of service requirement, added to hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period, and the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations (referencing § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew rules)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F003"],
        "scope_text": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F014",
        "references": ["29 CFR part 541", "§ 825.102", "§ 825.801(d)"],
        "statement": "If an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee (including FLSA-exempt employees), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001:F003"],
        "scope_text": "When determining whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and the 12-month employment requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": ["§ 825.300(b)"],
        "statement": "The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start; if an employee is on non-FMLA leave when reaching 12-month eligibility, any portion of leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after meeting the requirement is FMLA leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "prohibition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F004"],
        "scope_text": "Once an employee has been determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, and leave has already started.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may not",
        "modality": "must_not",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50 within 75 miles; eligibility is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave and is not affected by subsequent changes in employee headcount for that specific notice."
      }
    }
  ]
}

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to an employee of a covered employer seeking to be an eligible employee under the FMLA.
unit_attributes.choice_text: All three requirements must be met: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months, (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding leave commencement, and (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is defined as an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (subject to special rules for airline flight crew employees in § 825.801), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees working outside the U.S.).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided the rules in paragraph (b) are met.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2).
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2), employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, where an employee had a break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Either (i) the break in service is occasioned by USERRA-covered service obligation, or (ii) a written agreement exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where: (i) the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation (and the period of absence due to USERRA service must also be counted, without granting greater entitlement than USERRA), or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, the week counts as a week of employment; for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Employers may consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement, but if an employer chooses to recognize such prior employment, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees, in determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to FLSA principles for compensable hours of work based on actual hours worked; the determination is not limited by recordkeeping methods or inaccurate compensation agreements, and any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA principles may be used.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave for an employee returning from USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the absence due to USERRA service to meet the hours of service requirement, added to hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period, and the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations (referencing § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew rules).

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee (including FLSA-exempt employees), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start; if an employee is on non-FMLA leave when reaching 12-month eligibility, any portion of leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after meeting the requirement is FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Once an employee has been determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, and leave has already started.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50 within 75 miles; eligibility is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave and is not affected by subsequent changes in employee headcount for that specific notice.
